answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Echo Rule: each identity's action kernel (its per-epoch action mix) is committed and compared against its prior epochs. An identity whose actions diverge beyond a calibrated drift threshold from its own history is throttled and its weight decayed across the ocean of active agents. To farm N identities undetected, an attacker must maintain N distinct, internally consistent behavioural histories through every epoch—paying sustained compute and coordination cost per identity rather than a one-time registration fee.
